problem: Embedding-similarity object search (CLIP/SBERT) does not capture relational semantics such as containment or co-occurrence, while online LLM planners are too slow and costly for on-robot use. Neither handles interactive search well, where the target may be hidden inside closed containers.
motivation: Household robots must find objects efficiently using human-like priors, e.g. which rooms contain an object and which objects co-occur with it. Cosine similarity is a poor proxy for these priors (a milk carton looks similar to both a fridge and an oven). LLMs encode the priors but cost too much at inference time.
key_idea: Distill LLM room-object containment and object-object co-occurrence knowledge offline, via procedurally generated data, into small MLPs on frozen text embeddings, then use them to score 3D scene graph nodes (rooms, frontiers, objects) for utility-driven interactive search.
insight: Similarity distributions of SBERT, OpenAI and CLIP embeddings overlap heavily for positive and negative co-occurrence and containment pairs, while the learned scorers separate them. Room influence gives the largest SR gain (0.840 vs 0.876 with vs without, and it also lifts the embedding baselines). The utility margin Δ mainly improves SPL (0.219 to 0.282). Data scale (10% to 100%) and procedural diversity both matter, and the distilled models generalise to unseen and descriptive queries.
method: 3DSG construction: fuses RGB-D and pose into a semantic voxel map, BEV and occupancy maps, a Voronoi graph, and rooms split by doors, with frontiers and closed doors as unexplored nodes

Utility scoring: rooms are scored by p_contains, objects by p_co-occur, objects are then re-weighted by the parent room score u_r(w+(1-w)u_o) with w=0.3, and frontiers take the score of nearby objects or the room, or a default

Procedural LLM data generation: a hierarchy Household→Rooms→Categories→Objects with gpt-4o-mini yields 3824 object categories, 92K containment samples (continuous scores) and 7.5K co-occurrence samples (binary labels)

Distilled models: frozen SBERT embeddings of node and query are concatenated (768-d), and two 3-layer MLPs (512/256/128, 558K parameters each) are trained with MSE for containment and BCE for co-occurrence

Action selection: among actionable nodes with utility within Δ=0.1 of the maximum, pick the one with minimum geodesic distance; the node's affordance dispatches to A* navigation or an open-container manipulation policy

SymSearch benchmark: a symbolic scene-graph benchmark built on InteriorGS (1000 scenes) with semi-automated 3DSGs, manually annotated nested inside/on-top relations, and incremental reveal of rooms, frontiers and objects

setting.backbone: Frozen SBERT (22.7M) + two small MLPs (558K each) trained on gpt-4o-mini distilled labels
setting.model_size: ~1.1M trainable parameters (2 MLPs) on a 22.7M SBERT encoder
setting.training_data: LLM-generated data: 92K room-object containment and 7.5K object co-occurrence samples over 3824 object categories (gpt-4o-mini, ~3 h each)
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB-D + odometry pose, fused into an online 3D scene graph (YOLO-World segmentation in real world)
setting.action_space: High-level: choose a scene-graph node (frontier, room/door, container/object) to explore, executed with A* navigation and open-container manipulation
setting.simulator: Symbolic SymSearch (InteriorGS scene graphs), OmniGibson (BEHAVIOR-1K), and real world
setting.privileged: In SymSearch, ground-truth scene graphs and knowledge of when all rooms are explored; in OmniGibson, ground-truth segmentation and oracle 'magic open' manipulation; the real robot uses AR-marker-based pre-recorded opening motions

numbers.eval_set_note: 200 episodes across 10 InteriorGS scenes, 142 unique queries, N_max=50, averaged over 5 seeds

numbers_note: Real-robot success rate is reported only as '64%' over 36 trials, so it is not included as a numeric entry. The benchmarks are the paper's own, hence 'other:'. The split 'val' is a nominal label.
results: SCOUT reaches SR 0.876 / SPL 0.282 on SymSearch and SR 0.829 / SPL 0.415 on OmniGibson with ~0.1 s inference. This beats the best embedding baseline, SBERT (0.689/0.192; 0.632/0.241), and beats MoMa-LLM (0.827/0.255; 0.696/0.257) with gpt-5-mini, which needs ~295 s per episode. GODHS has a higher SymSearch SR (0.906) but a much lower SPL (0.159). The real robot succeeds in 64% of 36 trials, mostly limited by perception.
limitations: Depends heavily on scene graph and perception quality: duplicated or hallucinated objects and misclassified rooms cause most real-robot failures
Encodes generic household priors and does not adapt to household- or user-specific placements
Real-world evaluation is small (36 trials, one apartment) and relies on AR-marker pre-recorded manipulation; simulation results use oracle manipulation and segmentation
